newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel vows retaliation for any Syrian aggression.
newsitem.headline: Israel vows retaliation for any Syrian aggression.

text.p: Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai threatened "extreme" retaliation for any Syrian attack on Israel in an interview published on Friday.
"I don't believe that in the short range (Syrian President Hafez al-) Assad will make a grave mistake," Mordechai told Israel's Jerusalem Post daily.
But he added: "If you (Assad) carry out some military operation against us, you'll receive a very grave, extreme and immediate reaction from us. That is what I would tell him."

Syria's movement of thousands of troops in Lebanon last month from Beirut to near the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights caused war jitters in the Jewish state. The redeployment followed Israeli threats of retaliation for guerrilla attacks on Israeli troops occupying a strip of southern Lebanon.

Sporadic peace talks between the two countries since 1991 had foundered over the Golan, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, even before the election of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu last May froze prospects of further talks.
Syria wants Israel to return all the strategic plateau in exchange for peace. Netanyahu's hardline government has rejected trading occupied Arab land for peace.
